findings.description: In batchMint, the NudgePaid event (and the preceding nudgePaymentToken.safeTransfer to recipient, line 295) is emitted/executed AFTER the external nftMinter.mint(...) calls in the loop (line 281). Slither flags the event-after-external-call ordering. The nudge payout amount is snapshotted BEFORE the loop (line 274), the minter allowance is revoked before the transfer (line 284), and the contract uses SafeERC20; the nudge token is guaranteed != paymentToken. No value-bearing state is read post-call to size the payout, so the documented donate-forward / front-run-floor design appears intact -- but this is the nudge-pot payout path and the changed focus file, so it is retained for manual confirmation that a malicious/ERC777-style nudge or payment token cannot reenter batchMint (it is whenNotPaused, no nonReentrant guard) to double-dispatch the pot.

Return value of nftMinter.mint(_dispatcherIndex, recipient) is ignored inside the batch loop. The minted token id / unit count is discarded; batchMint relies purely on revert-on-failure semantics of the trusted minter. Corroborated by Aderyn 'Unchecked Return' at the same call. Low impact given the minter is owner-pinned and trusted, but it is the core batchMint emission path -- worth confirming the minter cannot succeed while minting zero units (which would let a caller clear the nudge gate via count >= nudgeSize without acquiring real NFTs).

Return tuple of INFTMinterV2(nftMinter).configs(_dispatcherIndex) is partially ignored: only the first element (dispatcher address) is destructured, the price/growthBasisPoints/other fields are dropped. Intentional here (batchMint only needs the dispatcher to derive primeToken), but flagged for completeness; no security impact identified.

Local variable nudgeAmount is declared without initialization and only assigned inside the conditional nudge-qualification block (lines 273-275). The default-zero is intentional and documented (nudge disabled / threshold not met / pot empty -> stays 0, which then clears any minReward==0 floor). Corroborated by Aderyn 'Uninitialized Local Variable' (line 280). Behaviourally correct in Solidity (zero-init); retained as in-scope nudge-logic noise, not a vulnerability.

External call nftMinter.mint(...) is made inside an unbounded for-loop driven by caller-supplied `count` (lines 280-282). Gas-bounded DoS / block-gas-limit exposure for very large count, and each iteration pays the dispatcher's ramping price. Caller-controlled and self-inflicted (caller pays), so impact is low; noted because it is the defining batchMint mechanic and the per-iteration external call is the surface the nudge gate (count >= nudgeSize) sits on.

CONTEXT-ONLY (NFTStaker is audit context, not the changed focus file). Slither reports reentrancy-no-eth across stake/unstake/claim paths where state (rewardBudget/committedDebt/user accounting at lines 514-517, 479-487) is written around external ERC1155/ERC20/_safePay calls; Aderyn raises a matching High 'Reentrancy: State change after external call' at NFTStaker.sol:445. NFTStaker uses OZ ReentrancyGuard per its spec, so these are expected to be guarded -- retained as a single representative entry so the deduplicator/code-scanner can confirm the nonReentrant coverage on every external-call-bearing path rather than re-derive the cluster. Not part of the BatchNFTMinter regression delta.
